concepts.learning_objective: Find common multiples of two numbers using the idli-vada game and the smallest number divisible by several numbers.
Find common factors of two or more numbers and relate them to jump sizes that reach every treasure.
Classify numbers as prime, composite or neither by counting their factors.
Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to list the prime numbers up to 100 and explain why it works.
Identify co-prime pairs as numbers with no common factor other than 1, using the safe-treasure game.
Relate the first common multiple of two numbers to their product when the numbers are co-prime.
Write a number greater than 1 as a product of primes and recognise that this factorisation is unique apart from order.
Find the prime factorisation of a product by combining the prime factorisations of its factors.

topics.title: Using prime factorisation for co-primes and divisibility

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether two numbers are co-prime by looking for a common prime factor in their prime factorisations.
Decide whether one number divides another by checking if its prime factorisation is included in the other's.
Use the last digit of a number to test divisibility by 2, 5 and 10 and to find remainders.
Use the number formed by the last two or three digits to test divisibility by 4 and by 8.

topics.title: Fun with numbers: special numbers and prime puzzles

concepts.learning_objective: Give reasons why a number in a group is special, using properties such as prime, composite, even, odd and square.
Solve grid puzzles in which prime numbers must give the stated row and column products.
